Logan, QLD

Shipping containers Logan

The yard is in Logan. 51-55 Bromley Street, Cornubia, with signage on the fence and containers standing in rows you can walk down. For a Logan delivery that means the cartage leg is fifteen or twenty minutes, a booking can be moved without it costing anybody a day, and you can come and inspect the exact unit you are buying instead of a photograph of one like it. What still takes planning is the far end, because Logan is seventy-odd suburbs and they do not deliver anything alike.

Common uses in and around town

Around Logan we deliver containers for plant, tooling and consumables kept on the industrial estates at Crestmead, Berrinba, Slacks Creek and Meadowbrook, tools and materials for the trades working the estate builds at Yarrabilba and Logan Reserve, extra room on small lots where the garage went back to the cars, gear lock-up for footy, cricket and scout groups around Beenleigh and Browns Plains, stock overflow for small businesses working out of a home shed, and feed, tack and machinery on the rural-residential blocks at Chambers Flat, Munruben and Carbrook.

The access problem in this district

The industrial half of Logan is some of the easiest work we do and there is no point pretending otherwise. The estates at Crestmead, Berrinba, Heathwood, Underwood, Slacks Creek and Meadowbrook were laid out for articulated vehicles, with broad entries and hardstand throughout. A container goes in there on a phone call and a gate code. The residential half is where the planning lives. Yarrabilba, Logan Reserve, Park Ridge, Flagstone and Greenbank repeat an identical set of problems street after street: a narrow carriageway with cars along both kerbs, one single position a rigid truck can work from which happens to be your frontage, comms and stormwater lids set into the crossing that will break under a loaded axle, and a turning head at the end of the cul-de-sac drawn around a garbage truck rather than something with six metres of container past the rear wheels. The blocks are cut and fill and eighteen months old, so the ground is still consolidating under thin turf. The older suburbs bring the opposite set. Woodridge, Kingston, Logan Central, Springwood, Daisy Hill and Shailer Park have short steep driveways that pitch away hard at the kerb, so a tilt bed grounds out before the container is clear, plus fifty years of gum and jacaranda over the road and side gates from an era of narrower mowers. A lot of those are lifts. Down on the river country at Eagleby, Bethania, Waterford and Loganholme the Logan and Albert flats are low, silty and slow to dry, and ground that looks firm on top can be soft two hundred millimetres down. Three photographs resolve nearly all of this: one along the street toward the house, one of the crossing and nature strip, and one of the intended position with whatever hangs above it in shot.

Grade moves the price more than size does, and it is what decides whether a unit is sold watertight — the full rundown is on the grades page.

Logan

Fifteen minutes from the yard

Being local is not a slogan here, it changes what we can do for you. A Logan address is a short run from Cornubia, which means next business day is genuinely normal rather than a best case, a delivery pushed by rain costs us a short trip rather than a full day of cartage, and if a container has to come back and be swapped for a different size or grade that is an inconvenience instead of an argument. Suppliers become flexible or inflexible depending on what a mistake costs them, and on a Logan job a mistake costs us very little.

It also means you can do the sensible thing and look before you buy. Come to 51-55 Bromley Street, Cornubia, Monday to Friday between 7:30am and 5pm or Saturday morning 8am to 12pm, and walk the rows. Swing the doors, sight down the floor, look at the seals and the corner posts, and put your head inside to see what light comes through. That is a fifteen minute drive from most of Logan and it removes every argument that normally happens after delivery. Ring 1300 467 776 before you come so the units you are interested in are standing where you can get at them, and so somebody is free to take you through the differences between grades rather than leaving you guessing.

On the ground

One usable stretch of kerb

On a new-estate frontage there is typically a single position where the truck can legally stand and safely work, and it is directly in front of your block. If two neighbours' cars are in it the delivery does not happen, because there is nowhere else within reach and no way to come back at it from the other direction. The same applies if the only route onto the property crosses a comms pit or a stormwater grate, since those are engineered for a car rolling over them, not for twenty tonne stopping on top. Cracked lids become the property owner's bill, not the driver's, which is why we ask about the crossing before we book a truck rather than after.

So there are three things we need from you and none of them are hard. Where can the truck legally stand, what does it have to cross to get onto the block, and what is overhead: power, comms, a verandah roof, a mature gum with limbs at four metres. Give the neighbours an hour's notice and clear the frontage. Mention at quote stage whether a pit or a grate sits in the crossing. Where a frontage simply cannot be worked, the fallback is craning off the road and over your fence. It is a bigger machine on the day, and the container lands first time, which on a cramped estate street repays the difference easily.

Worth knowing

Low ground at Eagleby, Bethania and Waterford

The Logan and Albert river flats run through a good slice of the city and they behave differently from the ridges. The soil is silt and old alluvium, it lets water go slowly, and a block that reads as dry on top can still be soft two hundred millimetres down a week after decent rain. Put a container straight onto that and it settles unevenly. Every bit of the load runs through four castings, and the moment they are no longer at a common height the frame starts fighting itself, the door end twists, and doors that opened with one hand need a shoulder behind them.

Fixing it is cheap and it lasts. Four concrete pads or hardwood sleepers beneath the corner castings, bedded down, then checked for level along the sides and across both diagonals, with the doors at the top of any fall so they swing the easy way. Lift the floor a hundred millimetres or so clear of the dirt so air can move under there and the underside is not pressed against damp soil for the next decade. That levelling is done on delivery wherever the site permits, so mention at quote stage that the ground is low, soft or on a slope and the timber comes up on the truck. Give some thought as well to where the unit sits in relation to the drainage the builder designed, because six metres of steel dropped across a flow path pushes water somewhere the landscaper never intended.

Common questions

Buying a container in Logan

Can I come and look at containers in Logan before I buy?

Yes, and it is the simplest thing you can do. The yard is at 51-55 Bromley Street, Cornubia, open Monday to Friday 7:30am to 5pm and Saturday 8am to 12pm. The units stand on hardstand, so you can swing the doors, sight down the floor, look at the seals and work out for yourself what a grade actually means. Ring 1300 467 776 first so the units you want to see are accessible and somebody is free to walk you through them. If you cannot get in, we will photograph the exact unit on request and send it through before delivery.

Can a truck get into a street at Yarrabilba or Logan Reserve?

Usually, provided the frontage is clear on the day. Cars line both kerbs out there, and a tilt-tray needs one particular length of kerb directly outside your block to work from. Service lids and stormwater grates in the crossing are the other constraint, since a loaded rear axle will break them. Get the cars shifted for an hour, describe the crossing to us beforehand, and most of these run smoothly. If the frontage truly cannot be used, a lift from the road over your fence can, and it is frequently the faster way in regardless.

How fast can you get a container onto a site in Logan?

Next business day comes up regularly, since the yard is at Cornubia rather than the far side of Brisbane. A plain 20ft heading somewhere with open access is the quick end of it. Time gets added by a crane booking, a modification such as a lockbox or vents, or wet weather on soft ground, where waiting a day is better than a truck buried on your block. Where the date is fixed by a settlement, a site start or removalists already locked in, say so up front and the run gets built around it.

Does a container on a residential block in Logan need approval?

That turns on three things: how long it is there for, whether it can be seen from the road, and what it is being used for. A lot of the newer estates also carry covenants tighter than anything the council requires. Nobody here is going to guess at the rule covering your particular street, and it is worth establishing before you order rather than afterwards. The shape of it is predictable enough to plan around. Short-term, screened and used for storage sits at the easy end. Permanent, prominent and modified is where questions get asked. Moving one later means paying for a second delivery.
